question: Where was the latest Regional Centre of the Sports Authority of India opened on 2 November 2020?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zirakpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The latest Regional Centre of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) was opened in **Zirakpur, Punjab** on 2 November 2020.
 
• Zirakpur is strategically located close to Chandigarh, making it accessible for athletes from various parts of North India.
 
• This new centre aims to provide **world-class training facilities** to athletes in the region.
 
• The establishment of this centre is part of SAI's efforts to **decentralize sports infrastructure** and provide more localized training opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sports Authority of India (SAI)**

 
 
• The Sports Authority of India (SAI) is the apex national sports body of India, established in 1984 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports of the Government of India.
 
• It is responsible for the development and promotion of sports in India, providing training facilities, coaching, and financial support to athletes.
 
• SAI operates various training centres and academies across the country, including the Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS) in Patiala, which is one of the largest sports institutes in Asia.
 
 
 
• **Regional Centres of SAI**
 
 
• SAI has several regional centres across India to promote sports at the grassroots level and ensure that athletes have access to quality training facilities close to their hometowns.
 
• These regional centres are equipped with modern infrastructure, including training grounds, gyms, and residential facilities for athletes.
 
• The regional centres also conduct talent identification programs and provide scholarships to promising athletes.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Sports Infrastructure**
 
 
• Access to good sports infrastructure is crucial for the development of athletes as it provides them with the necessary facilities to train and improve their skills.
 
• Quality infrastructure also helps in injury prevention and recovery, ensuring that athletes can train consistently and perform at their best.
 
• Investing in sports infrastructure is essential for nurturing talent at the grassroots level and building a strong foundation for future champions.
